title: probes-are-a-nest-with-settled-in-preprocess
intention: The shim's at-rest probes are shaken as a nest whose preprocess sieve, settled, hands the record band only the probes whose watched tree moved since they last fired, so a settled probe costs the beat nothing and a quiet beat reads no corpus twice.
how: (1) each Probe declares (or defaults) the root it watches — `root` on the frozen dataclass, defaulting to the class-space repo root for a probe that names none, so no probe fires less than today; (2) shim.on_pulse builds a nest from its declared probes: subjects = {identity: probe}, one preprocess sieve settled(subjects) -> the identities whose tree_fingerprint(root) differs from the fingerprint stamped at their last fire (or never fired, or while_true), one record sieve trigger(probe) that is today's body (fires -> _fire -> gathered_enough) unchanged; the shake replaces the for-loop at shim.py:260, the held/fired/still_true bookkeeping stays; (3) the fingerprint at last fire is stamped in the shim's own memory beside _was_true/_cleared — instance state the holder owns (Law 6), lost on restart like _cleared, so a restart walks once; (4) proofs: nest tooth over a fixture shim (settled trigger not called; moved and never-fired called), zero-reads tooth, shim proofs resealed unchanged, does_a_beat_cost_what_changed's before/after numbers on the verdict; all under netns.
falsifier: DONE when (1) the at-rest probes are assembled through cairn/tools/base/nest.py as a nest whose subjects are the discovered probes and whose one PREPROCESS sieve, settled, receives the whole probe set and returns only those whose watched root moved since their last fire (tree_fingerprint) or that have never fired; the record band fires each returned probe's trigger exactly as on_pulse does today — one tooth in cairn/tools/base/proofs/ over a fixture shim with three probes (one settled, one moved, one never fired) asserting the settled one's trigger is NOT called and the other two are; (2) a settled probe reads 0 files on the beat — measured by a tooth counting opens under a fixture root (strace-free: wrap Path.open / os.walk in the fixture); (3) the beat's wall time and file reads over the live 99 are measured before and after by does_a_beat_cost_what_changed (the existing probe) and the after reads fewer files on a quiet beat, with both numbers on the verdict — never a snapshot asserted in a proof; (4) the poke-per-crossing, while_true, cleared, enough, and first_seen semantics of on_pulse are byte-identical (the shim's own proofs reseal unchanged). RED if any probe's trigger fires less often than today when its root moved, or if a band is authored. WRONG INTENT if Akien wants every probe walked every beat regardless (his 'agreed on all counts' says settled probes are not walked).
traces_to: Law 1 (a probe re-deriving an unchanged corpus every beat is re-deriving the settled); memory shrinking-footprint-event-not-poll and ground-loop-is-just-the-heartbeat (the beat stays a pulse; the saving is in the shim's evaluation, not in the loop). Telos: the system's resting cost shrinks as it settles.

decisions.text: BaseShim.on_pulse shakes its declared probes as a nest: subjects keyed by probe identity; one PREPROCESS sieve `settled` returns the identities to score; one RECORD sieve `trigger` is today's per-probe body (shim.py:275-300) verbatim. The for-loop at shim.py:260 becomes the shake.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15 'agreed on all counts' on CC's proposal; measured 2026-09-16: ground_loop discovery.discover() finds 99 probes over 40 devices, 0 import failures (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/discovery.py:168); cairn/tools/base/shim.py:259-300 on_pulse evaluates every declared probe's trigger in turn each beat — the only skip is the in-memory _cleared set (shim.py:271, per shim, lost on restart); 48 of the 99 probe modules walk a tree (rglob/glob/os.walk/iterdir) in their trigger or carry; the memo tool cairn/tools/base/settled.py:86 settled(key, root, compute) — remembered until tree_fingerprint(root) changes, 5.9ms over 806 files — is used by 6 probes today and 42 walkers do not use it. (2026-09-15's note '~78 probes, Probe.settled() exists, none wired' is corrected by this measurement: it is the settled TOOL, and six are wired.)

decisions.text: settled returns a probe iff while_true, or never fired, or root is None, or tree_fingerprint(root) != the fingerprint stamped at its last fire. A settled probe's trigger is NOT called and it reads 0 files; it appears in the pulse record as held with reason 'settled — root unchanged since last fire'.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15: 'settled() exists and none are wired to it'; Law 7 (visible, never silent); settled.py:64 tree_fingerprint

decisions.text: Probe gains `root: str | None = None` — the tree it watches. A walking probe names its root at build (48 measured walkers); a probe that names none is never settled. No probe fires less often than today when its root moved.
decisions.by: CC 2026-09-16 unobjected; the hidden_assumption at birth (a clock- or bus-reading trigger must not be settled)

decisions.text: The last-fire fingerprint lives in the shim's memory beside _cleared and _was_true; a restart walks once. Persisting it is not built until a measured need.
Cleared is checked BEFORE settled: a retired probe is never fingerprinted.
decisions.by: shim.py:266-273 'CLEARED IS TERMINAL and is checked FIRST'

decisions.text: Measured done: beat wall time and file reads over the live probes on a quiet beat, before and after, read through does_a_beat_cost_what_changed and written on the verdict — never asserted as a number in a proof.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15 'agreed on all counts' on the before/after measurement; memory proof-over-live-data-assert-invariants

decisions.text: Depends on 71cd4a62e8c5 (the shake hands postprocess the stamps): the preprocess contract fire(name, subjects) -> subset is built there with a fixture sieve; this is its first live tenant.
decisions.by: Akien 2026-09-15: ticket order 'the shake ticket ... ahead of the probe-nest ticket'

why: 99 probes are evaluated every beat and 48 of them walk a tree to answer a question whose answer has not changed since the tree last moved — the beat re-derives the settled (Law 1) and the resting cost of the system does not shrink as it settles.
